builds.howItPlays: You spend Energy to tap Yasuo and shuffle a unit between its base and the battlefield, chaining several moves in one turn to dodge fights, resupply an ally, or grab a score no other line gets you. Units that care about moving reward you every time you relocate them, so a well-planned string of moves can swing a whole turn in your favor.
builds.whyYou: You like puzzles that live on the board itself, working out which unit to move first so the whole line still works by the last step. You enjoy planning three or four moves ahead and get a kick out of watching a sequence click into place turn after turn. If you don't mind a deck that asks a lot of you in exchange for flashy plays, Yasuo is built for that kind of player.
builds.ratingNotes: pace 7: riftbound.gg says the Chaos half 'plays at 100 miles an hour, looking to cheat energy', and the plan is to 'move units around the field to score two points per turn'. stance 7: the same guide describes actively 'finding units with an ability we can snowball' rather than waiting on the opponent, a proactive movement engine. complexity 8: hextechanalytics walks through a line where you 'move him to base normally, use the Legend to move him to another legal field, then Ride the Wind back to base... three moves for four Energy', and riftbound.gg admits the two domains 'don't mix up very well together', so sequencing is demanding. variance 6: riftbound.gg's win line depends on whether 'those shenanigans can last for four turns to reach 8 points', a real if-this-then-that swing, but hextechanalytics describes multiple parallel payoffs (scoring, draw, buffed units) that smooth out bad draws somewhat. Ability: pay 2 Energy and exhaust Yasuo to move a friendly unit to or from its base. Confidence: medium, only two sources were found and neither is a top-tier tournament report; riftbound.gg itself notes the deck is 'mostly played for fun' rather than for results, which the reviewer should weigh against the coordinates above.
